messages:
sara_support: FYI customer Acme (acct-1234) opened a ticket — embeddings cache behaving inconsistently. Batched requests are showing cache hits (fast) but identical single-item requests miss and hit backend (slow/costly).

sara_support: Repro steps they gave:

# single
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"input":"welcome to acme","model":"redwood-embed-1","prefix":"acme-prod-usr-42"}'

# batch
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"input":["welcome to acme","welcome to acme"],"model":"redwood-embed-1","prefix":"acme-prod-usr-42"}'

Single call: 220ms, cache miss. Batched call (2 items same string): 35ms, cache hit.

sara_support: They also saw some dimension mismatch errors intermittently when clients switch models quickly (not primary issue but might be related to cache keying). Logs attached from their request window (sanitized):

[2026-02-12T14:22:01Z] req=abc123 embed.get cache_key=emb:v1:acct-1234:prefix=acme-prod-usr-42:model=redwood-embed-1:dim=1536 -> MISS
[2026-02-12T14:22:01Z] req=abc124 batch.embed.get cache_key=emb:batch:v1:acct-1234:prefix_hash=sha1(acme-prod-usr-42):model=redwood-embed-1 -> HIT
[2026-02-12T14:22:01Z] req=abc125 embed.set cache_key=emb:v1:acct-1234:prefix=acme-prod-usr-42:model=redwood-embed-1:dim=1536

sara_support: Customer thinks we might be reusing prefix slots when batching, or that our cache key normalization differs between single vs batch code paths.

max_infra: pinging infra/runtime team. Can you dump the exact cache key formats for both single and batch paths? I want the server side logs around 14:22.

devon_sre: grabbing logs now. Quick note: we introduced a micro-optimization where batch path precomputes a prefix_hash and uses a unified batch key for dedupe across items — that might explain HIT on batch. Single path uses explicit per-item key built from ordered params.

devon_sre: logs from runtime (sanitized):

# single path
build_cache_key(namespace="emb", version="v1", acct=acct-1234, prefix=acme-prod-usr-42, model=redwood-embed-1, dim=1536) -> "emb:v1:acct-1234:prefix=acme-prod-usr-42:model=redwood-embed-1:dim=1536"

# batch path
build_batch_key(namespace="emb:batch", version="v1", acct=acct-1234, prefix_hash=sha1(acme-prod-usr-42), model=redwood-embed-1) -> "emb:batch:v1:acct-1234:prefix_hash=<sha>:model=redwood-embed-1"

max_infra: aha. So batch path uses prefix_hash (shorter) and not including dim. That could cause a hit if any item in batch matched an existing hashed entry regardless of dim. If downstream store stores per-item entries after batch expand, it's possible batch prefetch hit then returned cached vectors that don't match expected dim sometimes.

katya_ml: that would explain the dimension mismatch reports when clients flip model (1536 vs 4096). If cached entry was stored under a hashed batch namespace without dim, expanding it into per-item responses might incorrectly serve vectors of older model.

sara_support: customer reports most of their single requests are from a background job using model param order scrambled (they pass model after prefix sometimes). Could that affect key canonicalization? They also use trailing slashes in prefix occasionally ("acme-prod-usr-42/" vs "acme-prod-usr-42").

devon_sre: we canonicalize prefix for single key path (we strip trailing slash) but batch hash uses raw string -> different inputs map to different prefix_hashes. Also single includes dim, batch doesn't. Two problems.

devon_sre: immediate mitigation: toggle runtime feature flag embed_cache.strict_keying=true for acct-1234 to force batch and single to use identical canonicalization (no prefix_hash, include model+dim). I can flip for them for now.

max_infra: agree. Also add a guard: if cached item dim != requested dim -> treat as MISS and set after recompute (to avoid serving wrong vector). That should prevent dimension mismatch from leaking.

katya_ml: long-term: batch path should include model+dim in the batch key or expand and check per-item metadata before returning. I'll open an RFC for consistent key format.

sara_support: sent customer a note that we found an inconsistency and we're applying a temporary flag. They're okay with a toggle but want to know if this is a client bug or server bug.

devon_sre: it's a server-side optimization gone too far. Client hygiene helps (consistent prefix string, avoid changing model frequently without clearing cache) but we own the normalization guarantees. We'll fix.

sara_support: customer also asked for repro steps so they can test after flag flip. I suggested the following local test (mirrors their flow):

# baseline clear
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings/clear-cache -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"acct":"acct-1234","prefix":"acme-prod-usr-42"}'

# single -> miss
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":"hello","model":"redwood-embed-1","prefix":"acme-prod-usr-42"}'

# batch -> hit
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input":["hello","hello"],"model":"redwood-embed-1","prefix":"acme-prod-usr-42"}'

If single still misses after we flip flag, good sign.

max_infra: flipped embed_cache.strict_keying for acct-1234 at 2026-02-12T15:10:01Z. Please confirm with customer.

sara_support: customer tested @ 15:18 — reports consistent hits for both single and batch now. Latency normalized. They also ran the model-switch test and no more dim mismatch errors.

katya_ml: filed PR to unify keying across code paths: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4291 (adds model+dim to batch key, normalizes prefix before hashing, and verifies dim metadata on get). Marking as high priority.

devon_sre: follow-up actions:
- roll out PR #4291 to canary cluster (eng-runtime)
- add extra logging metric cache.dim_mismatch_rate for better signal
- docs: update embedding cache keying section and best practices for clients (canonical prefix format)
- support: send postmortem summary to customer and add KB article

sara_support: Customer very appreciative of the quick flag flip. They asked for KB link and to be notified when fix is in prod. I'll track.

api-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1799 (embed cache inconsistent keying -> temporary flag applied -> fix PR #4291 opened)

sara_support: closing ticket once we confirm PR in prod. Thanks all :tada:
